 In formal terms, S.’s ‘Stanzas’ adapt the Spenserian stanza by combining its rhyme
scheme and final alexandrine with fluent octosyllabics akin to the seven-syllable lines
of Lines Written among the Euganean Hills. There is also a marked influence from
Wordsworth’s ‘Ode: Intimations of Immortality’, in mood and some details of phrasing
but also in the use of the hexameter as an element of a lyric stanza (cp. the Immortality
Ode, lines 9, 18). S.’s octosyllabics are, like Milton’s in ‘Il Penseroso’, distinctive in their
fusion of light metrical movement with a tone of quiet and sometimes dark reflection,
recalling the use of similar effects in Act 1 of PU; and this too suggests an influence from
the passages including seven-syllable lines in Wordsworth’s Ode, particularly 180–7:
